note: sam_hdr_read calls sam_hdr_rebuild on the parsed header, which invokes sam_hdr_link_pg when pgs_changed is set
pgs_changed is set to 1 when PG header lines are parsed, so sam_hdr_link_pg is invoked
npg is the total count of PG lines; with multiple PG lines present, execution proceeds
pg_end is reallocated to npg entries, so valid indices are 0..npg-1

code: for (i = 0; i < hrecs->npg; i++) hrecs->pg_end[i] = i;
note: pg_end is initialized to identity mapping for all npg entries
For each PG line, the PP tag value is looked up in pg_hash to find the parent PG
When a PG line has a PP pointing to a missing program, ret is set to -1 but processing continues; the PG's prev_id remains unset
For PG lines with valid PP targets, chain_size is computed from the parent's chain size

code: for (i = j = 0; i < hrecs->npg; i++) { if (hrecs->pg_end[i] != -1 && chain_size[i] > 0) hrecs->pg_end[j++] = hrecs->pg_end[i]; }
note: Chain-end PGs (pg_end[i] != -1) with non-zero chain_size are compacted into the first j positions of pg_end
When no chain-end PG has a non-zero chain (j==0), the code reads pg_end[npg_end-1]. If npg_end (the old count from parsing) exceeds npg (the reallocated size), this is an out-of-bounds read

OOB read: pg_end was reallocated to npg entries but npg_end (the count accumulated during header parsing) can exceed npg when PG lines with PP to missing programs cause the removal logic to skip removals, leaving stale entries in pg_end beyond the reallocated bounds
